nodes.label: Generating timetables
nodes.rationale: Generation runs as a background job. The request chooses greedy or joint with solver.

nodes.label: Timetable generation
nodes.rationale: The Generate page queues a job and polls it. Choose joint when several divisions share faculty, electives cross divisions, or lab batches must run in parallel. Choose greedy for a single class or a quick draft.

nodes.label: timetable_jobs
nodes.rationale: Generation rows are claimed by flask workers run. See RUNBOOK.md. The job result can carry version_id, violations, rule_cost, and rule_costs.

nodes.label: Timetable generate API
nodes.rationale: POST /api/timetable/generate queues the job. GET /api/timetable/jobs/<id> is polled. The body may include solver, rules_override, and an optional draft label.

nodes.label: Greedy timetable solver
nodes.rationale: services/timetable/generator.py is the default. Classes run one after another. For each class it orders sessions, tries free slots, and picks the first teacher and room that fit. It keeps several candidates and ranks them with the quality model. Fast and dependency-free, and good when classes rarely share staff. A teacher taken by the first class is unavailable to the next, so later classes get the leftovers. With preferences on, candidates are ranked by quality_score minus 0.5 times rule_cost. The slot-by-slot loop is unchanged.

nodes.label: Joint CP-SAT solver
nodes.rationale: services/timetable/joint_solver.py builds one CP-SAT model for every selected class. load_problem turns targets into demands, solve places them, and persist_cohort archives old rows, retires them, and inserts the new timetable with lab_batch_group_id set for batch sessions. It runs for at most TIMETABLE_SOLVER_SECONDS, default 20 from the .env variable, and returns the best feasible solution. Unplaced demands are reported as unassigned slots. When ortools is not installed the job logs a warning and falls back to the greedy generator, so a deployment without the package still generates.

nodes.label: Shared solver inputs
nodes.rationale: Both solvers take a scope of one class, one course, or every class; working days and lecture length; subjects split into theory and practical, with electives from student_subject_selections; faculty from faculty_subject_allocations plus faculty_absences and faculty_unavailability; rooms whose room_type contains lab for practicals and the rest for theory, with capacity checked against the group; lab batches; and existing timetable rows outside the job so a teacher or room already booked is not booked again.

nodes.label: Timetable quality model
nodes.rationale: timetable_quality_service scores a timetable from 0 to 100 using clash risk, faculty fatigue, room overuse, and load balance. Both solvers are scored the same way so the Generate page can compare them. When max_hours_per_day or max_consecutive_hours is on, the model uses those thresholds for fatigue features.

nodes.label: Parallel lab batches
nodes.rationale: fill_parallel_batches places the other batches of a practical in the same slot with a different teacher and lab when it can, otherwise they take their own slots.

nodes.label: OR-Tools
nodes.rationale: CP-SAT is built with OR-Tools. The library is the ortools package in requirements.txt. Documentation: https://developers.google.com/optimization.

nodes.label: Joint solver hard rules
nodes.rationale: A demand is placed at most once. A teacher gives one session per slot across cohorts in the job, and none in slots already booked or marked absent or unavailable. A whole-division session excludes everything else for that division. Electives of different subjects may run together. Different lab batches may run together. The same elective subject or the same batch appears at most once per slot. A subject chosen across several divisions is one demand with several cohorts. Room capacity limits practicals to free labs and theory to free rooms. Exact rooms are assigned afterwards by _assign_rooms, largest group first. The same subject occurs at most twice a day per cohort and per batch.

nodes.label: Timetable preferences
nodes.rationale: Capability timetable_preferences. With it off, users do not see the rules below and both solvers keep the historical objective: avoid a subject repeating on a day (weight 10) and prefer earlier slots (1 per slot step). See DESIGN_CAPABILITIES.md.

nodes.label: Soft rule registry
nodes.rationale: services/timetable/rules.py is the single registry. Each rule has a weight from 0 to 20; 0 switches it off. Rules are faculty_preferences, max_hours_per_day, max_consecutive_hours, idle_gaps_students, idle_gaps_faculty, room_changes, spread_subject, lab_blocks_contiguous, no_first_hour_after_evening, lunch_window, prefer_early, and workload_max. default_rules() is the registry default. legacy_rules() is the pre-rules objective. effective_rules(cursor, institution_id, settings) picks one, merges a per-run rules_override, and says whether preferences count. Joint adds every weighted rule to the CP-SAT objective through _soft_terms. Room changes are scored only after room assignment. evaluate() scores any finished timetable. Both solvers return violations, rule_cost, and rule_costs, shown as Why these slots.

nodes.label: Legacy soft objective
nodes.rationale: legacy_rules() is the pre-rules objective, spread weight 10 and early weight 1, used when timetable_preferences is off.

nodes.label: Faculty window preferences
nodes.rationale: faculty_preferences holds one row per teacher window. faculty_id is faculty.user_id. day_of_week 1 is Monday. kind is preferred or avoid. weight is 1 to 5. APIs: GET and PUT /api/faculty/<faculty_id>/preferences, and GET and PUT /api/portal/preferences for the signed-in teacher. A teacher may only reach their own record.

nodes.label: Workload norms
nodes.rationale: Capability workload_norms, default off, with enforce soft or hard. A norm is a weekly teaching range in hours, min and max from 0 to 60, per designation, plus a default. Norms are stored in the institution timetable_rules row under the reserved _workload key, so there is no schema beyond revision 0016. rules.load_rules ignores underscore-prefixed keys and save_rules keeps them. limits_for resolves the norm from faculty.designation. weekly_hours sums live timetable rows. assess returns under, ok, over, or no_norm. Soft enforce costs weight times hours over the norm, default weight 6, counting hours inside the run and hours already taught outside it. Hard enforce caps joint placements at the remaining hours and makes greedy treat an over-norm teacher as unavailable. Minimums are never enforced by the solvers; they only flag. Nothing with a minimum is placed as a hard constraint. The faculty-workload report gains designation, norm_min, norm_max, workload_flag, and an outside_norm count. The teacher dashboard shows My workload from GET /api/portal/teacher, null when the capability is off.

nodes.label: Workload service
nodes.rationale: services/workload.py owns workload norms. GET and PUT /api/timetable/workload-norms. PUT is audited as workload_norms_changed. 404 capability_off when the capability is off. 409 rules_table_missing before revision 0016. 400 norms_invalid for hours outside 0-60, min above max, more than 40 designations, or names over 50 characters.

nodes.label: Timetable versions
nodes.rationale: Capability timetable_versions, default on once revision 0017_timetable_versions is applied. With it off, both solvers replace live rows directly and the version endpoints do not exist. With it on, a job first creates a draft covering every class in the job (timetable_versions and timetable_version_cohorts). Solvers write rows with is_active 0 and timetable.version_id set. The live timetable is untouched, so students, teachers, attendance, exports, the public API, and webhooks keep seeing the current timetable. In a multi-class greedy job, class N treats earlier draft rows as busy and ignores live rows the draft will replace (versions.busy_clause). Drafts beyond keep_drafts, default 10, are pruned oldest first. A draft that placed nothing is dropped. Publish copies active rows to timetable_history, retires them, and activates the version rows, one transaction per request. Classes with no rows are skipped. The timetable.published webhook fires per class with reason published. Rollback is publishing an archived version again. A manual slot added while a version is live is tagged with that version. Only drafts and archived versions can be discarded. Compare pairs slots as unchanged, room_changed, moved, added, or removed, and totals changes per teacher.

nodes.label: Timetable versions service
nodes.rationale: services/timetable/versions.py. publish activates a draft. diff compares two versions or a version against live. Reading needs timetable_versions_view, timetable_change, or timetable_generate. Changing needs timetable_versions_publish or timetable_generate. Versions are scoped to the caller's institutions. Endpoints cover list, detail, diff, publish, rename, and delete. Delete of the live version returns 409 version_published.

nodes.label: Manual timetable slots
nodes.rationale: services/timetable_slots.add_slot handles POST /api/timetable/slots. It checks holiday, division or batch clash through academic_rules/clashes.cohort_slots_clash, faculty clash and availability, and room clash. Error codes are slot_class_busy, slot_batch_busy, slot_faculty_busy, slot_faculty_unavailable, slot_room_busy, and slot_batch_invalid. DELETE /api/timetable/slots/<id> deletes a slot that has never been used. A slot with attendance or lecture sessions is retired (is_active 0) so marks are kept. Both endpoints need timetable_change.

nodes.label: Interactive slot check
nodes.rationale: services/timetable_slots.check_slot runs every manual-slot check without writing and returns faculty_id plus errors. add_slot calls it with first_only=True and raises the first error, so the grid predicts exactly what a save would refuse. exclude_id ignores one existing row so a slot can be checked against its new position. POST /api/timetable/check needs timetable_change. rule_cost from slot_cost is present only when the slot is clean and timetable_preferences is on. The Timetable page pre-checks up to 60 cells and shades them green, amber, red, or grey. Confirming a drop does DELETE then POST, so a slot with attendance is retired and the marks stay. Moves go onto an undo stack. GET /api/timetable also serves one teacher or one room. Print hides the controls with print:hidden.

nodes.label: Room bookings
nodes.rationale: Capability bookings, off by default, adds the bookings table in revision 0018 to the clash ledger. services/bookings.py is the only reader. A booking is one date or a weekly weekday until repeat_until, for an event, exam, maintenance, or an outside party. room_usage_for_week feeds approved bookings to both solvers in the same start/end shape as timetable rows. booked_room lets check_slot refuse a weekly slot that meets a weekly booking (slot_room_booked). A dated booking does not block a weekly slot, because the booking side already refused it if the slot existed first. create and decide refuse a live timetable clash (booking_room_busy) or another approved booking (booking_room_booked) and return free rooms of the same type. Only approved bookings block anything. With requires_approval, default true, a request waits as requested until a rooms_change_room holder of the owning institution decides. A bookings_change or rooms_change_room holder booking a room their own institution owns is approved at once. Sharing follows Institutions through candidate_rooms_clause. Decisions are audited as booking_requested, booking_approved, booking_rejected, and booking_cancelled. Notifications, when on, queue booking_request to approvers and booking_decision to the requester.

nodes.label: Lab batches
nodes.rationale: lab_batch_groups: every practical becomes one session per active batch of the division for the academic year that contains the week start date. See DESIGN_LAB_BATCHES.md.

nodes.label: DESIGN_LAB_BATCHES.md
nodes.rationale: Cited for how lab batches split a division's practicals.

nodes.label: DESIGN_CAPABILITIES.md
nodes.rationale: Cited for the capability flags that turn timetable preferences, and the related behavior, on or off.

nodes.label: RUNBOOK.md
nodes.rationale: Cited for how flask workers run claims timetable_jobs.

nodes.label: Reports documentation
nodes.rationale: docs/REPORTS.md is cited for the faculty-workload report, which gains norm columns while workload norms are on.

nodes.label: 0016 timetable preferences
nodes.rationale: Revision 0016_timetable_preferences stores timetable_rules, one JSON document per institution, and faculty_preferences. Workload norms reuse this row under the _workload key.

nodes.label: 0017 timetable versions
nodes.rationale: Revision 0017_timetable_versions. The timetable_versions capability is default on once this revision is applied.

nodes.label: 0018 bookings
nodes.rationale: Revision 0018 adds the bookings table used by the room-booking clash ledger.
